$schema_note: Machine-readable baseline of every version-dependent claim the cost-control bundle relies on. The cost-control-verify skill diffs the CURRENT Claude Code version's docs against this file, writes CHANGELOG entries, and patches the 'affects' targets. verdict/confidence are as-of baseline_verified_date. Edit via the skill, not by hand, so the changelog stays honest.
baseline_docs_version: 2.1.212 (pinned on first install 2026-07-17 via `claude --version`; supersedes the unpinned 2026-07-16 doc fetch)
baseline_scope_note: The 2026-07-17 v2.1.212 baseline pass RE-VERIFIED the 8 claims that govern executable guardrail behavior, each against a verbatim quote from a live doc fetch: spawn-gating-event, spawn-tool-input-schema, agent-frontmatter-hooks, nested-spawn-hooks, subagent-model-precedence, explore-agent-model, statusline-rate-limits, available-models-gate. The remaining 7 (workflow-size-config, telemetry-metrics, session-controls, output-styles, hooks-context-injection, usage-attribution, claude-version-cmd) govern PROSE, DASHBOARD, and DOC surfaces only — they were NOT re-fetched this pass (deliberate token frugality per the skill's cost note) and carry their 2026-07-16 verdicts forward UNCHANGED. claims.summary: Which hook surface can block a subagent spawn.
claims.current_value: RE-VERIFIED 2026-07-17 vs v2.1.212 docs — mechanism unchanged; two wording updates. A subagent spawn IS a PreToolUse tool call on the `Agent` tool. sub-agents.md VERBATIM: 'In version 2.1.63, the Task tool was renamed to Agent. Existing `Task(...)` references in settings and agent definitions still work as aliases.' PreToolUse is the ONLY hook surface that can block a spawn — hooks.md decision-control table VERBATIM: 'PreToolUse | hookSpecificOutput | permissionDecision (allow/deny/ask/defer), permissionDecisionReason' (NOTE: 'defer' is a 4th value not present at the 2026-07-16 baseline; the guards only ever emit 'deny', so no change needed). `SubagentStart` CANNOT block — the current wording is NOT the baseline's 'Shows stderr to user only' but hooks.md decision-control table VERBATIM: 'SessionStart, Setup, SubagentStart | Context only | hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext adds context for Claude. ... No blocking or decision control'; corroborated VERBATIM: 'For SessionStart, Setup, and SubagentStart, the exit code 2 stderr renders in the transcript as a <hook name> hook error notice ... Claude doesn't see it, and the session or subagent proceeds.' SubagentStart payload carries agent_id + agent_type only, no model (hooks.md 'SubagentStart input'). `TaskCreated` is the task-LIST event — hooks.md lifecycle table VERBATIM: 'TaskCreated | When a task is being created via TaskCreate' — unrelated to spawns; blocking it rolls back a todo item. (It also takes no matcher: 'TaskCreated ... don't support matchers and always fire on every occurrence'.)
claims.since_version: 2.1.63 (rename); 'defer' permissionDecision value present as of v2.1.212 docs
claims.verify: doc-fetch hooks.md exit-code table + sub-agents.md rename note; live: spawn fable subagent, expect deny entry in model-guard.jsonl

affects.what: PreToolUse-only blocking; SubagentStart observe-only; TaskCreated passthrough
guards on PreToolUse Agent|Task; SubagentStart/Stop logging only; NO TaskCreated registration

claims.summary: Field layout of the Agent tool's tool_input as seen by PreToolUse hooks.
claims.current_value: NOW PUBLISHED (verified 2026-07-17 vs v2.1.212 docs; was UNVERIFIED at the 2026-07-16 baseline). hooks.md 'Tool input schemas' section '##### Agent — Spawns a subagent' publishes the table VERBATIM: `prompt` (string), `description` (string), `subagent_type` (string, e.g. "Explore", 'Type of specialized agent to use'), `model` (string, e.g. "sonnet", 'Optional model alias to override the default'). This CONFIRMS the guards' primary probe paths .tool_input.model and .tool_input.subagent_type are correct; the .params.model/.opts.model fallbacks are now redundant but harmless. BONUS (PostToolUse): tool_response for a completed Agent call carries resolvedModel (v2.1.174+ — 'the model the subagent actually runs on, which can differ from the model value in tool_input'), totalTokens, totalDurationMs, totalToolUseCount, and a usage{} token breakdown — a documented surface for per-subagent cost attribution. NOTE: as of v2.1.198 subagents run in the BACKGROUND by default, so an omitted run_in_background yields status 'async_launched' and tool_response carries NO usage fields.
claims.since_version: 2.1.63 (tool); schema documented as of the v2.1.212 docs

claims.summary: Subagent frontmatter supports a `hooks:` key scoped to that agent's lifecycle.
claims.current_value: RE-VERIFIED 2026-07-17 vs v2.1.212 docs — unchanged. sub-agents.md 'Supported frontmatter fields' VERBATIM: '`hooks` | No | Lifecycle hooks scoped to this subagent. Ignored for plugin subagents'. CAVEAT confirmed VERBATIM: 'For security reasons, plugin subagents don't support the `hooks`, `mcpServers`, or `permissionMode` frontmatter fields. These fields are ignored when loading agents from a plugin. If you need them, copy the agent file into `.claude/agents/` or `~/.claude/agents/`.' — the bundle's agents install to ~/.claude/agents/, so the frontmatter gate applies to them.

claims.summary: Do settings.json PreToolUse hooks fire for tool calls made BY a subagent?
claims.current_value: RE-VERIFIED 2026-07-17 vs v2.1.212 docs — STILL AMBIGUOUS, verdict stays PARTIAL. hooks.md common-input fields VERBATIM: 'agent_id | Unique identifier for the subagent. Present only when the hook fires inside a subagent call. Use this to distinguish subagent hook calls from main-thread calls.' — implies settings-level hooks DO fire inside subagents, but no page states it outright for PreToolUse, while sub-agents.md positions frontmatter hooks as the per-subagent mechanism. Depth limit now CONFIRMED VERBATIM: 'Depth is counted as the number of subagent levels below the main conversation... A subagent at depth five doesn't receive the Agent tool and can't spawn further. The limit is fixed and not configurable.' The frontmatter-replicated gate covers nested spawns REGARDLESS of which reading is right, so this claim remains NOT load-bearing. NOTE (sub-agents.md, security): 'plugin subagents don't support the hooks, mcpServers, or permissionMode frontmatter fields' — so the frontmatter gate only covers agents in ~/.claude/agents/ or .claude/agents/ (where the bundle's are), NOT plugin-shipped subagents; those are covered by the settings-level PreToolUse gate if it fires nested, else ungated.

claims.summary: CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL is a highest-precedence override; =inherit == unset.
claims.current_value: RE-VERIFIED 2026-07-17 vs v2.1.212 docs — unchanged. model-config.md env-var table VERBATIM: CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL is 'The model to use for all subagents, agent teams, and the agents a workflow runs. Accepts an alias such as `haiku` or a full model name, and overrides the per-invocation `model` parameter and the subagent definition's `model` frontmatter. Set to `inherit` to use normal model resolution instead'. sub-agents.md resolution order: (1) CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL, (2) per-invocation model param, (3) frontmatter, (4) main conversation's model. inherit==unset as of v2.1.196 (earlier: inherit forced the main model). NEW since baseline (v2.1.211, applies to this install): 'A per-invocation `model` parameter also applies when the subagent is resumed or sent a follow-up message, so the subagent stays on that model. Before v2.1.211, resuming dropped the per-invocation value and the subagent reverted to its definition's `model` field or, without one, the main conversation's model.' => on v2.1.212 an explicit per-spawn model now STICKS across resume; the old silent upgrade-to-lead-model-on-resume cost leak is gone. Also: 'Claude Code checks the environment variable, per-invocation parameter, and frontmatter values against your organization's availableModels allowlist. It skips a value that resolves to an excluded model and runs the subagent on the inherited model instead.'

affects.what: comment telling user not to set it globally
env override mirrored in model resolution

claims.summary: Built-in Explore agent's default model (research said it stopped forcing Haiku ~2.1.198).
claims.current_value: CONFIRMED 2026-07-17 vs v2.1.212 docs (was UNVERIFIED/low at the 2026-07-16 baseline; the 2.1.198 research figure is now doc-backed). sub-agents.md 'Built-in subagents' VERBATIM: 'As of v2.1.198, Explore inherits the main conversation's model instead of always running on Haiku. On the Claude API, the inherited model is capped at Opus: a main conversation on a higher tier runs Explore on Opus, and a main conversation on Sonnet or Haiku runs Explore on that same model.' And VERBATIM: 'A user or project subagent named `Explore` overrides the built-in and keeps its own `model` field, so define one with `model: haiku` to keep exploration on a lower-cost model.' => the bundle's agents/explore.md (model: haiku) is EXACTLY the documented remedy, and is load-bearing on v2.1.212: without it, Explore would inherit this user's Opus/Fable lead session and explore at lead-model cost.

affects.what: custom haiku override; harmless if built-in differs

Presence rule VERBATIM: 'rate_limits: appears only for Claude.ai subscribers (Pro/Max) after the first API response in the session. Each window (five_hour, seven_day) may be independently absent. Use jq -r '.rate_limits.five_hour.used_percentage // empty' to handle absence gracefully.' — exactly the guard the scripts use. Colors VERBATIM: 'Colors: use ANSI escape codes like \033[32m for green (terminal must support them)'; capture VERBATIM: 'Claude Code captures your script's output instead of connecting it directly to the terminal, so tput cols and language-level width detection cannot read the terminal size from inside the script' => stdout is never a tty, so never gate colors on isatty (the scripts gate on CC_STATUSLINE_NOCOLOR only). claims.summary: availableModels hard gate + managed-settings paths + enforcement scope.
claims.current_value: model-config.md 'Restrict model selection': the allowlist applies to the main session model (/model, --model, ANTHROPIC_MODEL, resume), alias resolution, AND subagent models — 'the model field in subagent frontmatter, the Agent tool's model parameter, CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL'. Entries match a family alias (sonnet), a version prefix, or a full model ID. An excluded subagent value is SKIPPED and the subagent runs on the inherited model. enforceAvailableModels (v2.1.175+) extends it to the Default picker option. Managed paths (settings.md): macOS /Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/, Linux/WSL /etc/claude-code/, Windows C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\; managed-settings.d/*.json drop-ins merge alphabetically. Managed settings parse TOLERANTLY (invalid entries stripped with a warning; /doctor lists them); user/project/local files are STRICT (invalid file rejected as a whole). settings.md lists availableModels as settable in any scope, though model-config frames it as managed/policy — a user-scope allowlist is self-serve but also self-removable.
claims.verify: doc-fetch model-config.md restrict-model-selection + settings.md settings-files (RE-VERIFIED 2026-07-17 vs v2.1.212; scope + match rules unchanged). NEW v2.1.210 caveat, RELEVANT TO THIS INSTALL (permissions.defaultMode='auto' + Fable lead) — model-config.md VERBATIM: 'the classifier's Claude Sonnet 5 default applies only when the allowlist permits Sonnet 5. When it's excluded, the classifier runs on the session's model, which the allowlist already governs, or on an Opus model when the session runs on Fable 5.' => if the availableModels gate is ever placed and OMITS sonnet, the auto-mode permission classifier stops running on cheap Sonnet 5 and falls back to the session model (or Opus under a Fable lead) — a silent per-tool-call cost increase on every auto-mode decision. Any allowlist placed here should therefore INCLUDE sonnet. Decide alongside the fable lead-session tradeoff before placing the gate.

claims.summary: UserPromptSubmit and SessionStart can inject additionalContext.
claims.current_value: Both support hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext (or plain stdout). SessionStart is non-blocking; UserPromptSubmit injects alongside the prompt. SubagentStart also supports additionalContext (injected into the subagent's context) — available for a future per-subagent nudge.
/usage attributes recent usage to skills, subagents, plugins, individual MCP servers, each as % of total; 24h/7d toggle. Requires v2.1.174+.

claims.summary: How to read the installed Claude Code version.
claims.current_value: `claude --version` (or `-v`) prints a string containing the semver; no public `version` field guaranteed in session/statusline data (app.version available via telemetry OTEL_METRICS_INCLUDE_VERSION).
